item.title: Connecting Desktop AI Agents to Hugo with WebMCP Local Relay
item.description:
In our previous article, we implemented WebMCP support on a Hugo static site. By using the imperative document.modelContext.registerTool API, we turned a static blog into a programmable tool provider for AI agents—exposing tools like list_article_series, get_articles_in_series, and get_article_content.

Testing those tools in the browser’s developer console (F12) or via headless browser automation like Playwright worked as expected.

However, a fundamental limitation quickly emerged. I wanted to use the tools with a desktop coding agent. When you use desktop coding assistants and AI environments like Antigravity, Claude Desktop, or Cursor, they don’t live inside your browser tab. They speak the standard Model Context Protocol over stdio or HTTP/SSE. They cannot execute JavaScript inside an active browser tab on their own.

item.title: Adding WebMCP Support to Hugo Static Sites
item.description:
Model Context Protocol (MCP) isn’t new anymore, and it isn’t just another evolving standard. It’s widely adopted and considered a critical part of agentic AI. Server-side MCP is powerful, but what happens when an AI agent needs to interact with the web?

Until recently, when an autonomous agent browses a website, it behaves like a human looking at a screen: it scrapes the Document Object Model (DOM), parses accessibility trees, takes screenshots, and guesses which CSS selectors to click or forms to submit. This “UI actuation” approach is slow, brittle, token-expensive, and breaks the moment a CSS class or layout shifts.

item.title: Building a Model Context Protocol server for Azure
item.description:
The earlier article in this series introduced Anthropic’s Model Context Protocol. It presented an example of building a simple MCP server for use with the Claude desktop application. The hello-world example was a very basic implementation of an MCP server. In today’s article, we shall extend our knowledge of creating MCP servers to achieve more practical applications. We will build an MCP server to interact with Microsoft Azure resources.

Anthropic made bootstrap MCP server development easy by providing the create-mcp-server package. To get started, you need to install this locally as a tool.

item.title: Model Context Protocol by Anthropic for connecting AI models to data
item.description: A couple of months ago, Anthropic introduced and open-sourced the Model Context Protocol (MCP). MCP is the new standard for connecting AI models to external data sources and APIs more easily and consistently. With the advances in AI, models are becoming increasingly powerful in reasoning and quality. However, as text-completion machines, these models still lack access to real-time data. AI providers have worked around this using Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and tool calling. Every data source requires custom implementation, and every provider has a way of integrating tools with AI models. MCP addresses these silos by providing a universal, open standard for connecting AI systems with data sources.
